verdict: CONDITIONAL PASS for trusted-workflow operational guard; HOLD any claim of an unforgeable server guarantee using GitHubActions app_id alone.
scope: Read-only proposed security-model/source review; no API/provider calls, ref writes, protection mutations, builds or publication.

importantFinding.finding: Required check context plus generic GitHubActions app_id identifies the shared Actions app, not the trusted workflow/event that issued a check. Another writable workflow/branch can create a same-named check with that app identity; a same-name job check can also collide, including the skipped-job concern. A custom check solves accidental skipping of the intended attester, but does not bind the required check to that attester.
importantFinding.concreteBypass: A writer creates a new FF descendant of currentProd on another branch and a workflow/job named Quaked / Dev-qualified (or a checks:write workflow posting the custom context), obtains success from the same Actions integration, then pushes that SHA to Prod. Context+app matches despite SHA never reaching Dev. This is a source-policy counterexample, not a performed exploit.
importantFinding.consequence: Do not describe genericActions app pin as server-enforced Dev membership against workflow-capable writers. Enforce-admins also does not stop an administrator changing the protection configuration.

soundParts: Exact-SHA custom success posted only after BOTH web and mac matrix succeeded on Devpush is the correct trusted-source eligibility policy. Do not use a conditionally skipped attester job check as the required context.

Prod protection: enforce_admins=true, allow_force_pushes=false, allow_deletions=false; required exact context pinned to actual appID; no bypass actors. Dev nonforce/nondelete/admin enforcement preserves ancestry of genuinely attested Dev commits.

Local precommit blocking on attached Prod and fresh-remote prepush FF/Dev-membership guard prevent ordinary accidental misuse; normal Git push must remain nonforce. Explicit promotionSHA/dryrun is correct.

A commit cannot reveal which local branch it was authored on. The enforceable content rule is remoteProd advances FF only to a commit already in trustedDev history, not proof of where gitcommit was typed.

minimalHardeningChoices.choice: If repository policy trusts every workflow-capable writer
minimalHardeningChoices.action: Reserve the context, remove checks/status-write grants from nonattester jobs, minimize attestation job inputs, audit all workflow/event permissions and document this explicit trust assumption. It is an operational guard, not a hard workflow-origin boundary.
minimalHardeningChoices.limit: A writer able to add/run workflows can still use sharedActions identity; default read-only token settings alone do not prove per-workflow exclusivity.

minimalHardeningChoices.choice: If owner requires the literal hard server boundary
minimalHardeningChoices.action: Use a required trusted workflow rule bound by server to a protected workflow identity if this repository plan/API supports it, OR pin the required attestation to a distinct dedicatedGitHubApp identity whose token/key is unavailable to arbitrary repository workflows. The issuer validates exactDev membership and fullCI qualification. Prefer existing organization capability/App; do not silently create a new service or assume availability.
minimalHardeningChoices.limit: A dedicatedApp is materially more setup than one genericActions check; raise that tradeoff. Keep its credentials behind server-enforced trustedDev/environment policy, never reusable from arbitrarybranches/PRs; same-name Actions checks then fail appID pin.

attesterRequirements: Single Devpush-only post-success job, no always fallback that turns skipped/failed dependency into success; verify both dependency results explicitly before posting.

Per-job contents:read/checks:write only in attester. No tests, dependencies, untrusted artifacts or repository scripts execute with its write token. Fixed inline issuer code and literal context; head_sha from immutableevent, not artifact JSON or userinput.
Bind context details/summary to workflow/runID/sourceSHA/version and prerequisite run outcomes. Never accept generic/manual/user-supplied success or a customcheck at a differentSHA.

Failed/cancelled rerun policy must be explicit: do not leave a success falsely current after known contradictory later qualification. Never publish merely because an old success exists without reading intended qualification identity.

APIReadbackContract.providedState: Parent reports currently unprotectedProd, no rulesets, admin access. Not independently API-verified by this reviewer.
beforeClaimingEnforced: Read back Prod and Dev protection/rulesets after apply: exactcheckcontext+actualintegrationID, enforceadmins, force/deletefalse, no enabled bypass that permits ordinarywriters.
Verify existing protection/ruleset rules are preserved, not erased by replacing the policy body; API error/plan limitation fails closed and is recorded.
Inspect workflow permissions/trusted-workflow availability and selectedApp identity; server configuration alone with genericActions app does not remove the counterexample above.

Negative acceptance should use a separately owner-authorized disposable protected testbranch/repository for absent/wrong-app/spoofed context, nonDevSHA and nonFF updates; do not move actualProd to probe. Gitpush--dryrun is not evidence receive-side protection rejects an update.
Do not move Prod or publish now: no release SHA chosen; ancestry reconciliation and implementation qualification remain prerequisites.
